# Deckard 1.9.0 - a clearer Site Compare, several clicks per page, and base addresses saved in the file

Everything in this release is in **Site Compare**, plus a larger window. The Compare tab is laid out so the results are easier to reach, a page can have more than one click, and a pages file now carries the two base addresses with it.

## What is new

- **A clearer Compare tab.** The two sites each have a card (**Old site**, **New site**) holding the base address, the username and password, and how that site asks for a login. In baseline mode the old site's card greys out. The reports folder, baseline folder and site name are folded under **Folders and site name**. **Run comparison** turns into **Cancel** while it runs. **Clear baselines...** is red, so it is not mistaken for a routine button.
- **A summary after every run.** For example "12 of 15 pages match, 2 differ, 1 failed", with **Hide pages that match** to leave only the pages that need a look. The Status column shows a tick, a triangle or a cross as well as the row colour, and a column heading that is sorting the table shows an arrow.
- **Optional settings under the selected row.** The first visit, click, wait for and click wait boxes moved into a panel that opens under the page you select, with a **Close** button. A small cog in the **Opts** column marks a page that has any of them set.
- **Add click.** A page can now have several clicks. Press **Add click** in the panel for each extra one, give it an id or CSS selector, what to wait for and how long, and use the arrows to put them in order. They are made in that order, each waiting for its own results first. A failure names the click ("Click 2 of 3: Could not click id ...").
- **Base addresses are saved in the pages file.** **Save pages...** now writes the Old and New base address with each page exactly as it is in the table, so someone you send the file to gets the base addresses as well. Opening it fills both boxes. With no base addresses the lines are used as typed.
- **A warning when a password is missing.** If a site has a username but no password, **Run comparison** asks first ("A password has not been entered"). A missing password sends no login at all, which is why every page then fails with a refused login. Choose **Go back** to enter it or **Run anyway** if the site needs no login. In baseline mode the old site is not asked about.
- **Failures in plain words.** A login that is refused shows as "Failed: login refused" in the table. Hover over it for advice that names the old or the new site, followed by the full message the browser gave. The same is done for an address that cannot be found, a refused connection, a timeout, a certificate problem and no network. The full message is still in the report.
- **Very tall pages no longer fail.** A search that returns tens of thousands of rows can be too tall for the browser to photograph, which used to fail the page. Deckard now saves and compares the first 100,000 pixels and shows "(part)" after the visual diff percentage; if even that cannot be photographed it saves the top of the page and marks the visual diff Skipped. The elements are still compared for the whole page, and the report says what was left out.
- **Pages open in the order of the file.** Opening a file clears any sorting you had clicked, so the pages are in the order the file holds them, which is the order they run and are saved in.
- **Duplicate this page** is now in the right-click menu of a page.
- **A larger window.** Deckard opens at 1920 x 1080, or the size of your screen if that is smaller.
- **Shortcuts.** On the Compare tab **F5** runs the comparison, **Esc** cancels a run and **Ctrl+S** saves the pages file.

## Pages files

The pages file has two shapes now. With no base addresses and no extra clicks it is the plain list of pages it always was. When it holds a base address, or a page with more than one click, it is an object:

```json
{ "version": 2,
  "oldBaseUrl": "https://old.example/app/page/",
  "newBaseUrl": "https://new.example/",
  "pages": [ { "label": "Agent", "old": "agents.aspx", "new": "Agents", "oldStart": "home.aspx" } ] }
```

The extra clicks of a page are saved in a `then` list inside its first click. Files from earlier versions still open: their full addresses are cut down using the base address boxes, and the next **Save pages...** writes the new shape. The command line (`Deckard.exe site compare --pages ...`) reads both shapes and puts the base address in front of each page that needs it.

## Things to know

- **Older Deckards cannot open the new shape.** A file that holds base addresses or several clicks needs 1.9.0 or later. An older Deckard refuses it, and the TypeScript tool cannot read it either. A file without those stays a plain list that any version reads.
- **A newer file opens with a warning.** If a pages file says it was saved by a newer version than the one you are running, it still opens, with a note that some of its settings may be ignored.
- **Each click is made on both sites.** The same id or selector is used for the old and the new page, so it has to work on both.
- **"(part)" is a partial comparison.** A visual diff of 0.00% (part) says nothing about the rest of a very tall page.
- **The command line never asks.** The missing password question is only in the window. The command line takes passwords from its options or the `AD_*` environment variables, and does not prompt.
